THIS LAND ACQUISITION APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 06.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 LA.APP. NO. 103/2023 3  2025:KER:20536
JUDGMENT Dated this the 06th day of March, 2025

This is an appeal filed challenging the judgment and decree dated 25.03.2015 in L.A.R.No.183 of 2012 on the file of the IInd Additional Sub Court,
Thiruvananthapuram.
Appellants were the claimants in the said L.A.R.
An extent of 0.45 Ares of property belonging to the appellants was acquired for widening the Ulloor Akkulam - Kuzhivila road (Reach - 4).
Section 4(1) notification was issued on 12.12.2007 and an award was passed by the L.A.O. on 14.02.2011.
The Land Acquisition Officer had fixed the land value at Rs.2,26,792/- per Are.
Dissatisfied with the award, the claimant had filed a reference application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
In the said reference, the learned Sub Judge re- fixed the land value at the rate of Rs.24,17,100/- per Are.
This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking further enhancement.
2. Heard Sri.B.Ananthu, Advocate appearing for the appellants and Smt.Rekha C.Nair, learned counsel for the respondents.

3. It is brought to my notice that this Court had in L.A.A.No.687 of 2015 vide judgment dated 25.01.2016 which concerns the very 2025:KER:20536 same acquisition for the very same purpose,
enhanced the land value of Rs.24,17,100/- per Are as fixed by the reference court to Rs.30,18,413/-
per Are.
Appellants seek the same enhancement with respect to the property acquired from them.
A copy of the judgment dated 25.01.2016 of this Court in L.A.A.No.687 of 2015 is handed over to me for perusal.
I note that the purpose of the acquisition is the same and the property involved in both L.A.As. are situated in the same village.
Hence the appellants are also entitled to the very same enhancement.

Appellants shall also be entitled to interest and statutory benefits as envisaged in law.

However, in view of the order dated 15.11.2024, the appellants shall not be entitled to interest or statutory benefits for a period of 2193 days which is the delay that had been occasioned in filing this appeal.

Following the dictum as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amanullah Khan v. State of Haryana and another [(2022) SCC OnLine SC 1184], the appellants/claimants will not be entitled 2025:KER:20536 to any statutory benefits on the enhanced amount of compensation for the said period of delay.
